title: Pricing checkpoint: entitlement fallback rules and per-route rate-rule engine PRD
creator: Avery Kim
description: Purpose: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a deterministic entitlement fallback behavior and a per-route rate-rule engine that enables fine-grained quota/rate control, predictable billing reconciliation, and safe rollbacks during plan transitions. This ticket captures product requirements, edge-case handling, test scenarios, and rollout constraints for the first engineering sprint.
background: Customers and internal SREs have surfaced several failure and ambiguity modes when: (1) a customer’s plan changes mid-billing-cycle, (2) an attempted burst exceeds both per-route and global entitlements, and (3) the billing system lags the real-time metering service leading to temporary negative balances. Current heuristics are ad-hoc (soft-throttle vs hard-cutoff) and produce unexpected retries, throttles, and invoice disputes. We need a single source-of-truth PRD specifying fallback semantics and an extensible rate-rule engine to avoid manual reconciliations.
scope: In-scope: (a) Formalize entitlement fallback priority order (route-level rules -> plan-level entitlements -> grace credits -> fallback model variant). (b) Design a rate-rule expression language for per-route limits with inheritance and overrides. (c) Define billing reconciliation hooks and observable events for disputes. (d) Acceptance criteria and test matrix for transitions (upgrade/downgrade mid-cycle). Out-of-scope: changes to pricing tiers themselves, new UI for plan purchase flow (small console telemetry additions are ok).
out_of_scope: Upstream pricing changes, payment provider contract changes, new self-serve checkout UX beyond telemetry links.
requirements: 1) Deterministic fallback order documented and enforced by runtime: routeRule -> customerPlanEntitlement -> graceWindowCredits -> modelFallbackVariant. 2) Rate-rule engine supports: fixed token quota, sliding-window concurrency cap, weighted bursts, and per-caller overrides. 3) Metering emits canonical events (usage.increment, quota.exhausted, fallback.invoked) with customer-visible reason codes. 4) Billing reconciliation job can reconcile up to 72 hours of metering-lagged adjustments and produce line-item corrections. 5) Rollback policy: canary on 1% of customers and automatic fallback to previous rule-set on discrepancy >5% of expected invoice delta.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: - We will prioritize deterministic server-side enforcement over client-side best-effort handling to reduce invoice disputes. - Chosen rate-rule language is intentionally minimal to avoid complex parsing and to keep latency impact near zero. - We will not attempt optimistic local enforcement in SDKs for launch; SDK sigils introduced later. - Grace credits are capped per plan to bound financial exposure.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy rate-rule engine to staging + 1% of production customers with non-critical plans. Monitor key signals for 72h. Phase 2: expand to 10% after fixing issues. Phase 3: full rollout with a weekend maintenance window and billing reconciliation dry-run enabled. If invoice delta >5% for canary cohort, immediately roll back rule-set and open incident response.
metrics_and_success_criteria: Primary metrics: reduction in billing disputes (target -60% within 30 days of full rollout), accurate metering reconciliation (>=99.9% of events matched), percentage of requests that trigger fallback behavior (<0.5% normal ops), and no increase in p99 latency for token authorizations. Secondary: number of manual billing adjustments before vs after rollout.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Fallback order enforced end-to-end: routeRule -> planEntitlement -> graceCredits -> modelVariant. Verified with integration tests that simulate overlapping limits.
AC-2: Rate-rule engine accepts and validates new rule-set via API; invalid rules are rejected with clear error codes and do not go to runtime.
AC-3: Metering emits canonical events with reason codes; billing reconciliation job consumes events and produces a reconciliation report within SLA for a 72-hour lag window.

AC-4: Upgrade/downgrade mid-cycle behavior documented and implemented: entitlements prorated, graceCredits applied once per calendar month, and invoice line-items include original and adjusted usage with traceable event IDs.
AC-5: Canary rollout for 1% of customers shows invoice delta within expected bounds (<5%) and no regression in request latency (p99 not increased beyond 10% relative baseline).
AC-6: Automated unit and e2e test coverage for at least 85% of rule interpretation branches and fallback paths.
AC-7: Operational playbook created and attached, with runbook steps for rollback, customer communication templates, and billing adjustment process.

AC-8: End-to-end demo: PM/Eng/Finance walkthrough where a simulated mid-cycle downgrade triggers expected entitlement reduction, grace credit application, and reconciled invoice line showing adjustment traceable to event IDs.
qa_and_test_plan: - Unit tests for parser and rule resolver. - Integration tests between runtime, metering, and billing-reconciliation job using synthetic customer datasets. - Chaos test: inject 30-minute metering lag and validate reconciliation behavior. - Manual acceptance: Finance team runs a 1-month dry reconciliation using 100 canary customers' history. - Performance tests: measure p50/p95/p99 for token auth and enforcement in high-concurrency synthetic traffic.
monitoring_and_observability: Dashboard: per-rule hit-rate, fallback-invocations, queued-metering-events, expected vs reconciled usage. Alerts: >0.5% requests triggering fallback for >15m, reconciliation job failures, invoice-delta >5% on canary cohort. Traces: include rule_id and event_id in request traces.
open_questions: Q1: Should graceCredits be transferable between routes within the same customer? (finance prefers no).
Q2: When a model fallback occurs, do we apply a different metering multiplier for cost equivalence or keep raw token counts?
Q3: Do we expose the active routeRule id to customers in the Console for debugging?
